project-trajectory/scripts/gen_arch_map..notes: the cross-component edge CMP-007 -> CMP-006, declared per the architecture rule. THE OWNER-SIDE CELL NOW HOLDS A DESIGN ROW, and the standing no-design-row note it used to carry is withdrawn rather than merely deleted: LLR-180 names module_bindings beside symbol_findings, so the providing endpoint of this seam is answerable by a design row for the first time (LLR-023 answers only for the rendered arch-map splice/drift — exactly the artifact this contract DISCLAIMS — and LLR-080 for sw_graph/build_html;build_module_map, which is why neither could take it). project-trajectory/scripts/prompts.py.contract: The prompt LOADER seam (SN-032): `load(key, override)` returns one shipped template's text or raises a named `PromptError`; `fill(key, text, values)` refuses an unknown slot and a declared-but-unfilled slot rather than launching a silently empty instruction; `preflight(keys, overrides)` turns a missing template into a launch-time refusal instead of a first-session crash; `digest(text)` fingerprints a template over NORMALIZED line endings, so a CRLF checkout is not a change. `KIT_PROMPTS` is the declared key->file map and the only vocabulary a caller may use.
project-trajectory/scripts/prompts.py.notes: source: the templates are files under project-trajectory/prompts/, not code.

SR-157's obligation delivered as the reporting protocol every delivered checker honours, stated at check.py; crosses B-05.
project-trajectory/scripts/check.py.notes: A census of 430 emission sites plus a two-way drive of every shipped checker found the protocol already honoured: 141 of 158 per-finding sites name a location (11 population-level, 6 thin), no advisory anywhere reaches an exit code, and 12 of 14 checkers exit zero on an absent optional input and name it. This row states a delivered property, not new work.
project-trajectory/scripts/check.py.rationale:
Stated once: ten requirement rows each carry a fragment of this protocol as a secondary clause and none takes it as its subject, so a new checker can violate it without failing anything. SR-157 owns the row, being the one that already states the most of it - row-level attribution, a declared gate, and advisory classes never joining the exit code - and the one-definer rule makes a single owner mandatory.

The PROTOCOL is fixed here, never the DISPOSITION: per-class severity stays each requirement's own declaration, and fixing it here would over-constrain rows whose needs differ.

Two clauses are deliberately absent. "Every degrade is named, never silent" is not stated: SR-181's acceptance permits a silent degrade where no prior committed state exists while SN-008 forbids one, so stating it would red an Approved row on the day this one landed. And the closed set is four DISPOSITIONS, not twelve exact tokens: the delivered checkers spell those four with twelve labels, and this row states the contract they already honour, not a rename they do not.
